findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public IP and exposing the MySQL endpoint to the internet, where it is reachable by anyone who can reach the security group ports.
storage_encrypted = false means the RDS volume and its snapshots store catalog data unencrypted, so data at rest is exposed if the underlying storage or a snapshot is accessed.
The master password is supplied via var.password in plaintext and stored in Terraform state, and the master username is the well-known 'admin'; no Secrets Manager/KMS managed secret is used.

findings.issue_category: no IAM authentication or TLS enforcement
findings.description: IAM database authentication is not enabled and no parameter enforces require_secure_transport, so connections to the MySQL instance may be unencrypted in transit and rely solely on the static master password.

The EC2 user_data embeds the database master password (var.password) in cleartext; user_data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any process/user on the host and via ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute.

No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled and an SSRF on the web app could retrieve instance profile credentials and the user_data containing the DB password.
No root_block_device/ebs_block_device configuration with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance volume (which holds the dbinfo.inc file containing DB credentials) may be stored unencrypted.

The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", allowing full control of all S3 buckets, EC2, and RDS in the account; compromise of the web server yields account-wide privilege escalation.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised database host.

findings.issue_category: missing rule descriptions and broad scope
findings.description: The database security group is attached to a publicly accessible RDS instance and permits MySQL from the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application instance's security group, widening lateral-movement surface.
Ingress on port 3306 is allowed from the whole VPC CIDR instead of being restricted to the application server's security group, so any host in the VPC can attempt to reach the database.

skip_final_snapshot = true with no deletion_protection means the database (and its data) can be destroyed without recovery, which an attacker with RDS permissions (granted by the wildcard IAM policy) could abuse for destructive impact.
